To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“The automation is the problem, but the pilots are not the solution”.

CFIS accidents are “functional complexity” accidents that result from a complex sequence of automation functions that pilots are unable to detect or control due to a lack of relevant information and cues on the flight deck.
CFIS accidents are the result of a complex series of events and that these accidents cannot be mitigated by a single intervention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of flight deck systems that are able to cope with the functional complexity of flight deck operations.
understanding the nature of CFIS accidents, their causes, and their implications for flight deck procedures and training.
the design of flight deck automation systems that can be relied upon by pilots to perform the tasks for which they have been designed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
CFIS accidents are the result of the interaction of a number of factors.
these accidents were the result of a complex combination of factors, including the automation, the pilots, the flight deck environment and the aircraft.
CFIS accidents are not the result of a single factor or event but rather a complex interaction of factors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CFIS accidents were not the result of a failure to follow procedures, a failure to monitor, or a failure of the automation.
the automation and the flight deck environment are not sufficiently “human centered” for these rare but catastrophic events.
“CFIS is a complex, multi-faceted, rare and difficult-to-anticipate failure mode that is not easily addressed by a single intervention or solution”.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the automation is the primary source of risk in these accidents.
the automation functions in the modern airliner cockpit have evolved beyond the ability of the pilot to monitor them.
the design of flight deck automation must consider the full range of possible failures and the full range of pilot interventions to mitigate these failures.
